subject: Request: SLA credit eligibility & issuance for 2027-06-10 outage

Subject: Partial outage morning of Jun 10 — SLA credit request

Hi Ava / Marissa,

Reporting a service disruption impacting our inference endpoints between ~02:15 and 09:05 UTC on Jun 10 (we observed elevated 5xxs and request timeouts; our traffic shifted to a fallback regional pool). This degraded our throughput and caused several customer-facing errors. We flagged in our runbook and have an internal timeline (attached).

Per our contract (SLA section), we believe this qualifies for a service credit. Can you confirm eligibility and estimated credit amount? Our billing contact is in copy (it@halocean.com).

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Blanchard

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: ava_chen@redwood.example, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:40:13 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Partial outage morning of Jun 10 — initial calc

Internal notes and preliminary calc (forwarding Sophie’s timeline).

Summary of incident window (from service logs):
- Start: 2027-06-10T02:12:40Z (first error spike)
- Full restoration: 2027-06-10T09:05:12Z (latency and 5xxs normalized)
- Total degraded window: ~6h 52m (412 minutes).

Contracted monthly uptime target: 99.95% (SLA doc section 3).
Assume full calendar month minutes = 30 days * 24 * 60 = 43,200 minutes.
Available uptime during month = 43,200 - 412 = 42,788 minutes.
Observed uptime% = 42,788 / 43,200 = 99.046% (~0.904% below target).

SLA credit policy (per SLA):
- < 99.95% and >= 99.0%: 10% credit of monthly invoice for impacted product tier
- < 99.0% and >= 95%: 25% credit
- < 95%: 50% credit

Prelim credit band: 10% credit (observed is ~99.046%).
If Halocean’s June monthly invoice = $120,000 (placeholder until Sophie confirms), estimated credit = $12,000.

Attachments: halocean-incident-timeline.csv (from customer).
Action items:
- Ava: confirm invoice amount with customer (Sophie).
- Rishi/Finance: please confirm this is an approvable credit band and whether we need additional sign-off for a $12k external credit.

-Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example>
To: markus_klein@redwood.example, finance-ops@redwood.example
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:02:58 -07:00
Subject: Request for approval — Halocean SLA credit (prelim $12,000)

Markus / Finance Ops —

We have a verified incident window for Halocean on 2027-06-10 that yields an uptime of ~99.046% for the month (see attached internal calc). Under our SLA schedule that maps to a 10% credit. Using the customer-provided spend (~$120k/mo) the credit would be ~$12,000.

Please confirm:
1) Approve issuing a 10% credit against June invoice (credit note ID draft: credit-note-HLN-20270616.pdf).
2) Any additional approvals required above $10k? (policy says finance lead signs >$10k).

If approved, I will prepare the credit note and DocuSign package and loop in the customer billing contact.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra

Markus Klein

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.example>

Subject: Re: Partial outage morning of Jun 10 — SLA credit request

Hi Sophie — thank you for the timeline and patience. Per our investigation and finance approval, Halocean is eligible for a 10% service credit for June.

What we’ve done:
- Verified the incident window against service telemetry and your timeline.
- Applied SLA credit policy: 10% credit of impacted product monthly invoice.
- Draft credit note prepared (credit-note-HLN-20270616.pdf) and DocuSign package ready for signature: https://docusign.com/link/abc123-credit-notice

Next steps for you:
1) Confirm the June invoice amount we should apply the credit to (we used $120,000 as a placeholder). Reply with the correct figure if different.
2) Sign the DocuSign packet (link above) to accept the credit note.

If you’d like, we can also apply the credit as an immediate invoice adjustment instead of a standalone note — tell me your preference and billing contact.

Apologies again for the interruption. We’ve pushed a mitigation to reduce the likelihood of the same failure mode and will include this incident write-up in the monthly reliability digest.

Best regards,
Ava Chen
